generated_by: hand. tools/vault_keys.py applies it to the loot_by_band of every dungeon vault and bank vault in data/dungeons.json (idempotent) and prices the items in data/dungeon_greed.json
owner_brief: The owner, 2026-10-21: "any feather or legendary item that gates a mon should be put into dungeons as vault reward chance".
what_this_is: The legendary gate items as CHANCE rewards in the dungeon vaults. One stack per pool in a vault's loot_by_band[band]: {"one_of": [{item, weight}, ...], "chance": c}, the form tools/dungeon_puzzles.py loot_table already emits (ONE pool, rolls 1, so a chest holds at most one item of a pool). Nothing else about a vault changes.
band_rule: A band is the first whose highest cap is at or above the player's RCT cap at the rip (data/dungeons.json engine.bands_why), so a band holds every player from its LOWEST cap up. An item goes in a band only if that band's lowest cap is at or above the cap its gate implies (tools/economy_sim.py CAP_BY_BADGES: gym5_cleared -> 45, gym8_cleared -> 60, champion_cleared -> 100). So gym5 items start at band 4, not band 3 (band 3 holds caps 40 and 45: a player with four badges), gym8 items at band 5 and champion items at band 6. tools/vault_keys.py refuses a pool that breaks it.

gym5_cleared.source: docs/mechanics/LEAGUE_LEVEL_CAP.md section 2; data/research_station.json economy.items kubfu_scroll gate_why

champion_cleared.source: docs/mechanics/LEAGUE_LEVEL_CAP.md section 2 (cap 100 once Blue has fallen)

chance.q_why: A chance of 2% a chest for one item, at the 4-chest vault every vault is normalised to: 1 - 0.98^4 = 7.8% a vault run, a median of 8 runs for one named item, a mean of 13. DESIGN numbers, one knob. The owner asked for 'a few runs'; one named item among up to 17 at band 6 cannot be both 'a few' and a chest that is not mostly keys, so the per-item rate is 2% and the pools are sized from it (a pool's chance is q x its weight sum / the base weight). Per chest: 4% at band 4, 12% at band 5, 31% at band 6 that SOME key item is in it, about 1.2 key items a band 6 run.
chance.chests_normalised: A 3-chest vault (the Night Shift's pay office, Starfall's instrument store) rolls each pool at 1 - (1 - c)^(4/3), so the odds per RUN match a 4-chest vault. A bank vault is 4 chests (data/dungeon_extras.json bank_vault.defaults.chests).

price: Each item is a data/dungeon_greed.json items row at cp 1, source 'unpriced', the same placeholder the Rare Candy carries. Three reasons it is not the bank price: (1) the bank buys none of them (data/bank.json never_buy names the feathers; the base bank lists only the four feathers and they are removed; no other item is in the base bank, grep of base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobbledollars/bank.json); (2) the wishing well refuses every 'unpriced' row (tools/dungeon_extras.py priced_ids), so a thrown key cannot be turned into netherite: a $5,000 feather price would make a well throw pay out about $4,500 of it, and would also cap the chance at about 2% a chest by itself because every chest already sits at 85-92% of its budget; (3) the clock charges a chest's EXPECTED value, and a key item is not wealth. The cost is the one the owner chose: more vault runs. If the owner would rather price them, the well's refusal needs an explicit key-item list first.
